checks_run.procedure: Direct source review of the round-8 to round-9 diff (d84d11a6..d974011f; the interrupted round-9 reviews did not finish it) and of the round-9 to round-10 diff (d974011f..cde60365), with an attempt to break D-226 to D-232.
checks_run.command: git diff d84d11a6..d974011f -- apps packages; git diff d974011f..cde60365 -- apps packages docs/api; reads of versions.ts, rules.ts, digests.ts, deep-links.ts, tasks/routes.ts, RulePage.tsx, ui.tsx, worker handlers/notifications.ts and sensitive-children.ts, integrations/routes.ts, access/sensitive-reach.ts
checks_run.expected: No served column, response, notification channel or write path names a hidden record, and no token sequence loses or misplaces a hidden literal; every mutation keeps its authorization, If-Match and audit.
checks_run.actual: Tokens (versions.ts:443-472). resolveRestrictedTokens runs after the If-Match check (updateVersion: requireIfMatch, then current.version !== expected gives 409, then status draft) and inside the same transaction, on the row locked FOR UPDATE. A token is resolved only if its <version> equals the locked row's version; any other version is 422 stale, and a non-token or unknown position is 422 marker_unknown. A create resolves against null, so every marker is refused. createVersion copies content server-side, so tokens never cross into a new draft. The tests cover the edits, grant changes and concurrent saves (logs 43, 46). Exfiltration: validateContent's refusals carry no value (conditionInvalid has no arguments). Condition operators are exact equality (eq/neq/in) plus decimal-only gt/gte/lt/lte (conditions.ts), so a dry run gives at most an equality oracle that needs a known candidate uuid (UUIDv7, 74 random bits); there is no prefix or ordering oracle. Audit events of a version update carry the raw conditions, but listAuditEvents redacts hidden ids in changes (audit/routes.ts:85-89). Observation, not a defect: a token names a row version, not a row id, so a hand-crafted API call could send rule X's token to rule Y at the same row version. It would resolve to Y's own literal at that position, which the writer could place with Y's own token anyway. This discloses nothing; the UI never does it (VersionPanel is keyed by version id; one open draft per rule; the URL fixes the version number). Notifications: the inbox list, mark-read and digest read all go through restrictedNotifications + restrictedNotificationView. The only other API reader, admin listNotificationDeliveries, serves ids and statuses but no text. The worker fan-out re-checks link, params, target and work item (restrictedForRecipient) and sends inbox.restricted with a home link. Search does not index automation rules. My Work and the workspace header redact work items (presentWorkItems). Web: the editor holds {from, draft}, saves with ifMatch: form.from, reloads from the saved response, and after 409 or stale 422 reloads GET /versions/n and shows workflowsP5.rules.changedReapply (en and ar present). Round-8 to round-9: maskRestrictedIdsInFields on run, write and failure keys and error text; restrictedNotifications on the inbox and the deep-link resolver; correctiveCasesOfActions. I found no gap.

checks_run.procedure: Judge D-229 (connector configuration names stay cannot-name) and D-228 (4) (cross-organization ids out of scope), as the assignment asks.
checks_run.command: reads of integrations/connectors.ts (toConnector :400-401, :710-711), integrations/routes.ts (CONNECTOR_READ vs CONNECTOR_CONFIGURE, shownRuns, shownActionable), access/sensitive-reach.ts restrictedIdsAmong (:511 markedInOrganizations)
checks_run.environment: Repository at HEAD; integration logs (both locales)
checks_run.expected: A reader never learns a hidden id they could not already see.
checks_run.actual: Not a defect, so no finding. D-229: credential_refs are SecretRef names ({provider, name}) from IT's manifest; they are never record ids, and the values are never served (only credentialRefViews). field_mappings are {source, target}: the target comes from a catalogue, and the source is a column name a connector administrator types. A source can name a sensitive record's uuid only if a connector configurer deliberately types it; that is an admitted person writing free text, the same as any comment field, and not a system disclosure. connector.read holders already see that configuration. Run error text and actionable-error params ARE masked (shownRuns, shownActionable), so a source value echoed into an error is masked for a reader not admitted. D-228 (4): restrictedIdsAmong limits its decision to the records marked in the reader's own organizations (markedInOrganizations, sensitive-reach.ts:511). The route-inventory sweep case 3b passes in both locales (shard-4 logs: 'case 3b unauthorized (other organization): 312 eligible operations swept', statuses 403 x70 and 404 x242, nothing persisted). So a cross-organization id can appear only as a value that an admitted writer typed, and it opens nothing for the reader. I accept both rulings.

summary: PASS. F-DG6-540 and F-DG6-541 are CLOSED_VERIFIED, and so is F-DG6-580, which is the same defect as my round-9 observation 601; observation 600 is covered under 540. The round-8 and round-9 reproductions pass on this candidate, with the token literals moved to the version-bound form. A new browser probe passes in en and ar: the double save keeps the hidden literal, and the concurrent edit gives 409, then the 'changed, re-apply' banner and a reload, and the re-apply keeps it. All 8 mutants are caught; M6B passes the textual sweep but fails the integration test. Every required check ran and passes: build, typecheck, lint, format, openapi (932), no-cdn, pnpm test on Node 22 and 24, integration twice (LANG unset and C.UTF-8), and the historical DG5-DG1 validation. Several first runs failed for environmental reasons, all disclosed: ENOSPC on a disk shared with the other reviewers, OOM kills, and timeouts under load. Each affected file or shard passes when re-run alone and unmodified. D-229 and D-228 (4) are accepted. I raise no new finding.
